messages:
eva: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a compact Playground chat header. Goal: shrink vertical chrome, keep streaming progress clear, and make Stop/Regenerate easier to find.
sam: Nice. Can you drop the mock here? Want to see how token counter fits.
eva: Uploaded a static mock + streaming gif: https://figma.example/compact-header (mock is intentionally tight)
kim: Quick a11y flag: the pale token counter has low contrast. We need >= 4.5:1 for body text. Otherwise VoiceOver users can't pick it up.
matt: Agreed. Also worried about discoverability on mobile — if we move controls inline they might be too small to hit.
eva: Two alternatives I built:
- Inline compact: Stop + Regenerate right next to timestamp + tiny token pill
- Overflow menu: small icon opens dense menu with Stop/Regenerate, Copy, Pin prompt
ana: My vote is overflow menu for mobile, inline for desktop. But copy needs to be explicit — people confuse the icon states.
sam: UX nit: instead of label "Stop" use "Stop generation" on hover/tooltip and aria-label. Short primary button can stay "Stop" visually.
kim: +1. Also ensure keyboard shortcut is documented in tooltip: e.g., `Esc` to stop, `Cmd+K` to rerun? Make sure aria-keyshortcuts matches.
eva: Proposed aria snippet for Stop button:
```
<button aria-label="Stop generation" aria-keyshortcuts="Esc" role="button">Stop</button>
```
matt: Small design ask: token counter should show two modes — per-response tokens (small) and session total (toggle). We should avoid always showing huge numbers.
ana: Could we collapse session total behind hover or click? Maybe show only per-response + a subtle total badge.
kim: For screen readers, announce when streaming completes and read out final token delta. Something like: "Streaming complete — 142 tokens generated." That helps when users rely on speech.
sam: Copy tweak: replace "Regenerate" with "Regenerate response" in tooltips. Keeps intent clear for new users.
eva: Also thinking about visual streaming affordance: a thin progress bar under the last message bubble vs a spinner in header. Which is less noisy?
matt: Progress under bubble is contextual and scales with message; header spinner can be missed when long chat history scrolls.
ana: Agree with bubble progress. But for very short replies header spinner helps. Could we show both depending on viewport height?
kim: Ensure progress indicator has `aria-live=\"polite\"` updates so screen readers don't spam users while streaming.
designbot: Reminder: document keyboard focus order when compact header collapses. Add to the spec and handoff package.
eva: Action items:
- kim: propose color tokens and a11y contrast fixes (PR)
- matt: test hit targets on mobile and suggest size minimums
- ana: prototype overflow menu for mobile + inline desktop
- sam: update copy strings for tooltips and ARIA
- designbot: add focus order and keyboard flow to spec
ana: I'll prototype overflow by EOD Wednesday and share screens.
sam: LGTM. If we can get a quick accessibility smoke test after kim's PR, we can merge the copy and close the iteration.
eva: Thanks all — will update the figma and ping when ready :thumbsup:
